## Synthesis Overview

This PR reconciles documentation and prompt files with the active Python-native orchestrator implementation across four files: `README.md`, `docs/planning/python-native-migration/prd.md`, `prompts/agents/story-orchestrator.md`, and `prompts/skills/story-pipeline/SKILL.md`. The three models broadly agreed on the PR's scope and quality but diverged on specific findings. Two majority findings identify incomplete reconciliation of stale "services" references, and one high-confidence singular finding (broken ADR 008 link) requires fixing before merge. Several singular findings were correctly identified as pre-existing issues or false positives upon verification.

## Consensus Findings

### ★★☆ Majority Findings (Two of Three Models Agree)

#### [M-W-01] README project structure tree still says "Use cases and services"

Severity: Warning
Category: Documentation
File: `README.md`
Lines: ~157–167
Detail: The Architecture section at the top of README.md was correctly updated from "Use cases and services" to "Use cases and strategies", but the deeper ASCII project structure tree still reads `├── application/ # Use cases and services`. This is the exact inconsistency the PR set out to fix — the services layer was retired per ADR 008. A reader scanning the tree will see the stale label.
Models: Qwen ✓ (as S-02), GLM ✓ (as W-01), Kimi ✗
Dissenting view: Kimi did not mention the tree; instead suggested adding a parenthetical note to the Architecture section (which was already updated).
Suggestion: Update line ~157 in the project structure tree from `│   ├── application/             # Use cases and services` to `│   ├── application/             # Use cases and strategies`.

#### [M-W-02] PRD Goal 5 still references retired `src/application/services/`

Severity: Warning
Category: Documentation
File: `docs/planning/python-native-migration/prd.md`
Lines: ~24
Detail: Goal 5 states: "Build a Python orchestrator that executes the story generation pipeline phases sequentially, calling `src/application/services/` directly in-process." This directly contradicts the Superseded Decisions section added by this same PR, which explains that ADR 008 retired the services layer and the orchestrator now calls `src/tools/` directly. The Non-Goals section and Tool Execution section were updated, but Goal 5 was left unchanged. A reader encountering Goal 5 before Superseded Decisions will see an uncorrected statement of intent that was never implemented.
Models: Qwen ✓ (as S-01), GLM ✓ (as W-02), Kimi ✗
Dissenting view: Kimi did not flag this specific stale reference in the PRD Goals section.
Suggestion: Update Goal 5 to reference `src/tools/` directly. Add a parenthetical note: "(Originally planned to call `src/application/services/`; superseded by ADR 008 — see Superseded Decisions.)"

## Divergence Analysis

#### [D-01] Topic: Phase 9 FinalEditorAgent dispatch status

Qwen says: Nothing — does not raise Phase 9 as an issue.
Kimi says: Phase 9 is presented as active but the orchestrator "does not actually dispatch it in the headless slice that runs in production." Recommends adding a "not yet dispatched" annotation (W-02).
GLM says: Nothing — does not raise Phase 9 as an issue.
Assessment: Kimi's claim is a **false positive**. The user context explicitly states: "FinalEditorAgent IS actively dispatched by the orchestrator per `docs/features/story-orchestrator.md` ('Phase 9 now executes real editing work through FinalEditorAgent'). The Kimi reviewer W-02 claim that it is 'not dispatched' appears to be a false positive." Kimi likely misread the orchestrator source or conflated loading with dispatch.
Resolution: Exclude Kimi W-02 from consensus counts. No action required.

#### [D-02] Topic: Phase 7b scene-writer branch validity

Qwen says: Nothing — does not raise Phase 7b as an issue.
Kimi says: Phase 7b incorrectly describes a `scene-writer` branch that the active orchestrator never takes. Recommends updating to reflect that the orchestrator always dispatches `chapter-writer` (W-01).
GLM says: Nothing — does not raise Phase 7b as an issue.
Assessment: Kimi's claim is **out-of-scope for this PR**. The user context states: "The scene-writer tool branch in Phase 7b is pre-existing spec text describing a config-gated path; the active orchestrator may or may not take it. This is existing documentation, not introduced by this PR."
Resolution: Exclude Kimi W-01 from consensus counts. If the scene-writer path is truly dead, a follow-up issue should clean it up separately.

#### [D-03] Topic: Phase 7f critique-runner vs quality-reviewer naming

Qwen says: SKILL.md Phase 7f lists `critique-runner` while the orchestrator references `quality-reviewer`. Rates as Warning (W-01).
Kimi says: Nothing — does not raise this.
GLM says: Nothing — does not raise this.
Assessment: **Out-of-scope for this PR**. The user context states: "The `critique-runner` vs `quality-reviewer` naming in SKILL.md Phase 7f is pre-existing; the PR only added the ⏳ marker without changing the underlying text." Qwen correctly identified the inconsistency but it predates this PR.
Resolution: Exclude Qwen W-01 from consensus counts. Consider a follow-up issue to align SKILL.md subagent names with orchestrator dispatch names.

#### [D-04] Topic: Severity of README project structure tree issue

Qwen rates: Suggestion (S-02)
GLM rates: Warning (W-01)
Assessment: GLM's Warning severity is more appropriate. The PR's stated goal is reconciliation; leaving the most visible project structure diagram stale undermines that goal. Readers scanning the README will see the tree before they read the Architecture section prose.
Resolution: Adopt GLM's Warning severity for the consensus finding (M-W-01).
